text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- INTEREST RATES SHOULD FALL IN FEBRUARY

Central Bank President Gustavo Loyola said Brazil's Monetary Policy Committee would lower the bank's basic interest rate, known as the TBC, when it meets tomorrow, indicating the government is not worried about the pace of economic growth.
-- COFFEE, ORANGE JUICE FUTURES CLOSE HIGH IN NEW YORK
Coffee and orange juice futures contracts closed high in New York due to a scarcity of coffee on world markets and a freeze in Florida.
-- BRADESCO BANK POSTS 824 MLN REAIS PROFIT
Bradesco, Latin America's largest retail bank, posted an 824 million reais profit last year, 52.6 percent over 1995. Bradesco's profit margin was 15.1 percent, the best in a decade.
O GLOBO
-- RIO DE JANEIRO CONSUMPTION ON THE RISE
Consumer consumption in Rio de Janeiro reached 30 billion reais in 1996 and grew at a faster rate than anywhere else in Brazil, according to a new poll.
-- LOSS IN ILLEGAL DEBT DEAL SEEN AT ONE BILLION REAIS
The government could have lost up to one billion reais in an alleged illegal issue of nine billion reais in debt securities.
-- CLINTON STARTS SECOND TERM PROMISING NEW ERA
U.S. President Bill Clinton began his second term in office asking a Republican-dominated Congress to help him launch a new era by turning the United States into a new promised land.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
--- BRASILIA ALREADY TALKING ABOUT $8 BLN '97 TRADE GAP
The government is already talking about an $8 billion trade deficit for 1997, $2 billion more than official estimates last month.
-- VOTE ON RE-ELECTION MIGHT COME ON JAN 29

The government could wait until Jan 29 to call a lower house vote on a bill that would allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to run for a second term. The vote was originally scheduled for Wednesday but the government must still woo PMDB members in the states of Goias, Para and Paraiaba.
* Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--John Miller, Sao Paulo newsroom, 5511 248-5414
